newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan financials rise on likely state buying.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan financials rise on likely state buying.

text.p: Taiwan's heavily weighted financial shares rose at mid-morning on Wednesday on what brokers suspected was state buying to boost market confidence.
After 90 minutes, at 0230 GMT, the financial sector was up 4.87 percent, while the main index had risen 2.23 percent.
China Development Corp, one of Taiwan's leading venture capital and investment firms and an affiliate of the ruling Nationalist Party, was up T$4 or 3.41 percent to T$121.
Farmers Bank had jumped by the daily seven percent limit to T$47.

"It's obvious the government does not want to see the index stay below 8,000 points. Buying the heavily weighted financials is the most effective way to boost share prices," said Chen Han-chung, an analyst of Yungli Securities.
